extraction.name: CoNLL-2003 Shared Task: Language-Independent Named Entity Recognition
extraction.description: The CoNLL-2003 shared task dataset for language-independent named entity recognition, covering English and German. The data includes training, development, test, and large unannotated files for each language. Four types of named entities are annotated: persons (PER), locations (LOC), organizations (ORG), and miscellaneous (MISC). The English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus (news stories between August 1996 and August 1997), and the German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus, specifically from the Frankfurter Rundshau newspaper.
extraction.creator: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang and Fien De Meulder, CNTS - Language Technology Group, University of Antwerp
extraction.publisher: CNTS - Language Technology Group, University of Antwerp
extraction.citeAs: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang and Fien De Meulder. 2003. Introduction to the CoNLL-2003 Shared Task: Language-Independent Named Entity Recognition. In Proceedings of CoNLL-2003.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus, consisting of Reuters news stories between August 1996 and August 1997. For training and development set, ten days' worth of data were taken from the end of August 1996. For the test set, texts were from December 1996. The preprocessed raw data covers September 1996. The German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus, specifically from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundshau. Training, development and test sets were taken from articles written in one week at the end of August 1992. The raw data were taken from September to December 1992.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: English data: Reuters Corpus (http://www.reuters.com/researchandstandards/). German data: ECI Multilingual Text Corpus (http://www.ldc.upenn.edu/), specifically articles from the Frankfurter Rundshau newspaper.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: English: training/development data from end of August 1996, test data from December 1996, raw data from September 1996. German: training/development/test data from one week at end of August 1992, raw data from September to December 1992.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Linguistic preprocessing was applied to the raw data: a tokenizer, part-of-speech tagger, and a chunker were applied. Two basic language-specific tokenizers were created. The English data was tagged and chunked by the memory-based MBT tagger. The German data was lemmatized, tagged and chunked by the decision tree tagger Treetagger.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Named entity tagging of English and German training, development, and test data was done by hand at the University of Antwerp. MUC conventions were followed. An extra named entity category called MISC was added to denote all names not in the other categories (including adjectives like 'Italian' and events like '1000 Lakes Rally'). The IOB tagging scheme was used (words tagged with O are outside named entities, I-XXX for words inside, B-XXX when two entities of same type are adjacent). Named entities are assumed to be non-recursive and non-overlapping; when embedded, usually only the top level entity was annotated.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotation was done by hand at the University of Antwerp.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: MBT memory-based tagger (for English POS tagging and chunking); Treetagger decision tree tagger (for German lemmatization, tagging and chunking).
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes named entities covering persons (PER), organizations (ORG), and locations (LOC) extracted from news articles.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The MISC category is very diverse, including adjectives (e.g., 'Italian') and events (e.g., '1000 Lakes Rally'). Data is drawn from news sources in specific timeframes (Reuters 1996-1997 for English; Frankfurter Rundshau 1992 for German), which may limit domain and temporal representativeness.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Named entities are assumed to be non-recursive and non-overlapping; when named entities are embedded, usually only the top level entity is annotated. Data is limited to two languages (English and German) and specific news domains.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, development (parameter tuning), and testing for language-independent named entity recognition systems. The shared task organizers were especially interested in approaches that made use of resources other than the supplied training data, such as gazetteers and unannotated data.
